messages:
alex: quick sync — infra asked us to land the per-tenant dashboard metrics schema this week, they need runtime-side RPCs and a contract by EOD tomorrow
maya: thanks. which runtime signals exactly? latency p50/p95, tokens-per-request, kv-cache-hit?
ryan: also need route-level QPS and queue-length for throttling decisions. and model-variant fallback counts.
joan: noisy neighbor detection wants per-tenant CPU/GPU utilization buckets + steady-state tail latency spikes. sampling ok, but we need stable tenant id mapping (no PII)
alex: agreed. infra wants minimal cardinality keys: tenant_id, route, model_id, region, host_pool. no user ids.
sam: question on quotas — do we compute quota usage in runtime or in the console (aggregated ingest)? if runtime, we'll need an auth header on internal metrics RPCs
ryan: runtime-side enforcement already reads token_id for quota checks. for metrics ingestion we can emit metrics with tenant_id only; quota computation can run in metrics pipeline for dashboards but runtime should keep a live counter for hard limits.
maya: UX note — console wants per-customer single-pane summary + expandable runtime traces. we should expose both aggregated and raw-sample views. retention for raw samples should be 7d, aggregates 90d.
joan: privacy check — PII scrubber must run before any raw-sample leaves runtime. no prompt text, only hashes for prompt signatures.
alex: API debate: do we add a new internal endpoint POST /v1/metrics/tenant_events or extend existing /v1/telemetry with tenant param? pros/cons?
sam: new endpoint simpler to version, clearer ACLs. existing telemetry is messy (mixed infra/customer).
ryan: downside: more endpoints to instrument on runtime and add retries. but I prefer new endpoint for isolation.
maya: console team prefers single ingestion stream so rollups are in one place. can we have ingestion facade that merges both?
joan: facade sounds ok as long as authentication & RBAC enforce per-tenant visibility. also need feature-flagged rollout (canary by org id).
alex: canary plan: 5% of orgs -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days, with automatic rollback on increase in error-rate or 2x unit-cost. add canary tags in events.
sam: deploy-bot: deploy queued for runtime change 1748123600 by @ryan :rocket:
ryan: quick schema draft (pseudo):
```
POST /internal/v1/tenant_metrics
{
  "tenant_id": "org_123",
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model_id": "redwood/7b-q",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "host_pool": "dedicated-01",
  "metrics": {
    "tokens": 120,
    "latency_ms": 230,
    "kv_cache_hit": true
  },
  "tags": ["canary:v1"]
}
```
maya: looks good. add field "sampled": true/false and "sample_reason" for raw-sample explanation.
joan: also add "scrubbed_prompt_signature": "sha256:..." (nullable)
alex: final concerns: cardinality explosion if teams attach freeform tags. enforce tag allowlist server-side.
sam: infra will reject events with more than 5 tags and deny freeform tag names unless registered.
ryan: tracing: we should include trace_id so console can join logs/traces with request timeline. no trace payloads.
maya: okay, next steps: ryan will land runtime endpoint + scrubber. infra will add accept/deny rules and canary selector. console will prototype dashboard widgets for summary+raw sample. joan will run privacy review.
joan: noted, I'll queue privacy review and list required docs.
alex: action items in short: ryan: PR for endpoint + tests (due tomorrow noon), sam/infra: ACL + tag allowlist (due tomorrow EOD), maya: dashboard proto (due +2 days), joan: privacy signoff (due +3 days).
ryan: I'll ping in #eng-oncall when canary starts. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks all — keep notes in the RFC thread and we'll meet if any blocker shows up. :eyes:
